title: dedicated-fleet-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-v29: smoother tokenbucket smoothing + throughput guarantees
author: Ethan Brooks
release_notes: Improve dedicated fleet autoscaler burst smoothing to reduce oscillations under flash traffic; add throughput guarantee metrics and per-fleet tokenbucket smoothing tunables; expose utilization reporting per-pool for billing and SLOs.
description: Motivation: customers operating Dedicated fleets observed oscillatory autoscaler behavior during flash bursts which caused transient latency spikes and excess scaling churn. This PR implements a smoother tokenbucket smoothing algorithm, tighter throughput guarantee checks to avoid over-provisioning, and richer utilization reporting so operators can diagnose burst utilization vs steady-state load. Summary of changes: 1) introduce tokenbucket_smoother with configurable half_life and max_slew parameters to the fleet autoscaler; 2) add throughput_guarantee predicate to autoscaling policy to reserve headroom for latency-sensitive classes; 3) emit new metrics (redwood.fleet.tokenbucket_smoothed_rate, redwood.fleet.throughput_guarantee_violation, redwood.fleet.utilization_by_pool) and wire them into Console dashboards; 4) add CLI and API flags for per-fleet smoothing and guarantee thresholds; 5) add end-to-end integration tests and unit tests; 6) update docs and release notes. Design notes: tokenbucket smoothing operates on the autoscaler's observed qps time series; we apply an exponential decay smoothing (configurable half_life) and apply a capped slew rate to changes to avoid sudden scale-downs. Throughput guarantees are checked before scaling decisions and trigger a short-term temporary capacity reservation when violated to protect latency SLOs. Backwards compatibility: default smoothing parameters preserve current autoscaler behavior; all feature gates are disabled by default for existing fleets. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-9821 - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests in perf-canary - [x] console dashboard updates - [x] docs updated - [x] changelog entry
commits: feat(autoscaler): add tokenbucket_smoother with half_life and max_slew parameters
perf(autoscaler): use smoothed rate for scale decisions and cap downward slew
feat(metrics): export tokenbucket_smoothed_rate and throughput_guarantee_violation metrics
feat(api): add per-fleet smoothing and guarantee flags to FleetConfig API
test(autoscaler): add unit tests for smoothing and guarantee predicate
docs: document smoothing and throughput guarantee configuration
ci: add perf-canary integration job for burst scenarios
review_comments: Ava Chen: Can we add an escape hatch config that disables smoothing per-fleet? Some enterprises want immediate scale-down for cost reasons.
Ethan Brooks: Added per-fleet flag 'smoothing.enabled' and documented tradeoffs in autoscaler.md. Default remains enabled=false to preserve existing behavior.
Priya Patel: The throughput guarantee predicate looks good; please ensure it doesn't interact poorly with burst credit accounting in Dedicated billing.
Ethan Brooks: Added a safety check in billing pipeline to treat temporary reserved capacity from guarantees as 'headroom' and excluded from long-term billing; noted in release notes.
Lars Nielsen: Unit tests cover downward slew but not combined smoothing + guarantee cornercase where both fire rapidly. Suggest adding end-to-end test with mixed priority traffic.
Ethan Brooks: Added perf-canary scenario 'burst_tokenbucket.yaml' simulating mixed priority traffic and validated behavior; results attached in CI artifacts.
notes: This PR reduces scale oscillations observed in customer fleets during flash events and provides operators new signals to tune autoscaler behavior. Operators should review the new smoothing defaults and consider enabling smoothing on fleets that experience elastic traffic. The throughput guarantee feature should be enabled only when latency SLOs are required; it will reserve short-lived capacity and may increase temporary costs.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: temporary increased reserved capacity may raise costs for fleets that enable throughput guarantees. Mitigation: defaults keep guarantees off; added billing exclusion for short reservations and metrics to surface cost impact.
